title: The event loop: call stack, task queue and microtasks

videos.script:
JavaScript does one thing at a time. {{one}} One line, then the next. There is no second worker in your program running alongside the first.

And yet a page plays a video, answers a click and waits for a server, all at once. {{how}} How? By never waiting. Instead of standing still until the server answers, a script asks, leaves a function to be called later, and finishes. The browser keeps the list of what to call, and calls each one when its turn comes. The thing that does that is the event loop.

{{why}} You need to know how it works for two reasons. The first is order. A timer set for zero milliseconds and a promise that is already resolved both run later, and one of them always runs before the other. You will see which, and why.

{{freeze}} The second is freezing. While your code runs, nothing else can: not a click, not a frame of animation. A loop that takes two seconds is a page that is dead for two seconds. Today you will freeze one on purpose, and then fix it.
